name: Luxurious Private Quiet Home NearMain St Cupertino
description: LUXURIOUS APT IN QUIET NEIGHBORHOOD–Beautiful newer construction with hardwood floors, granite countertops, stainless steel appliances and spa-like bathroom. Enjoy the convenience of a one-bedroom private furnished residence with full kitchen, living room, backyard & much more (including your own washer and drier in the home).  Near many new restaurants by Main Street Cupertino with easy access on/off freeways (280 and 85) and Expressway (Lawrence) from property. Super clean home.
host_about:
My husband and I have lived in Cupertino for over 20 years.  We are glad to call Cupertino our home as we enjoy the mild year around climate and the cultural diversity of the area.  With the mild weather, we look forward to having fruits and vegetables grown on the property year around.

In 2009, we purchased this home to allow a parent to live with us when the time is right.  Until then we have a fully furnished private apartment (attached to the main house, but fully separate full unit that is approx. 550 sq. feet).  The apartment can be used by someone while traveling or working in the Bay Area.  We have enjoyed staying in high end hotels and tried to create an ideal space that we personally would enjoy staying at while traveling.

One of our life goals is to travel the world.  We still have many many places to see!  In the meantime, we enjoy reading and hearing about places that we should visit!  The San Francisco Bay area has so many fun things to do that I sometimes think there just aren't enough hours in a day :)  

Wishing you a safe travels and memorable experiences.  As we want your stay to be enjoyable, please feel free to ask me any questions regarding the apartment.

description: Our warm, inviting family home is great for women who want to feel safe in a quiet neighborhood in the heart of Silicon Valley. host_about:
Hi!  I'm your host, Deb.  I love to explore new places, foods and cultures.  I'm married to John.  He's more of a homebody, but very funny and entertaining.  

Fun fact:  I'm a twin with a boy and I have girl-boy twins.  Our girl went to UC Davis and now she's a preschool teacher in Davis.  Our boy went to UC Santa Cruz and now he works at Waymo in Mountain View.  (You'll be staying in our daughter's room.)

At our home we let our guests choose their own desired level of involvement with us.  Some do their own thing and others become extended members of our family.  I particularly like to host dinners 'in honor of' previous guests who come back to visit (while other guests are here).  It's always a fun time.  For homes I co-host, I am always just a phone call or a short drive away.  

My first career was in candy: Hershey, Brach's, then Mauna Loa Macadamia Nut Company covering nut with chocolate. I did National Sales, Data Analysis, and Marketing. Then I moved into education. I was a substitute teacher and then I created and taught a course called Jump Start Your GPA. name: The Bangalore House & Oasis @ SJC
description: The Bangalore House is centrally located in the historic Rose Garden area. Enjoy the quiet Oasis, yet only minutes from SJC airport, freeways (101, 880), restaurants, cafes, mall, train, Avaya & Levi's stadiums, SAP & Convention Centers, downtown, Silicon Valley companies. Relax in a private room furnished for business leaders and discerning travelers. Many original paintings give the home an art-museum feel. Bonus amenities: refreshing black bottom pool, relaxing hot tub, sunny deck, hammock.
host_about:
I have just ventured into Airbnb and aim to make the world more hospitable by opening up a beautiful room in my lovely 1930s house for travelers across the United States and around the World. Within one month I have had the pleasure of hosting over a half dozen guests from New York, Los Angeles, Pennsylvania, China, Japan, Spain.  I enjoy hosting people that are professional, clean, and respectful, and treat my home and room with the same care they would treat their own home.


What is being offered here is a well-furnished room with a queen bed and a bathroom for exclusive use of the guest(s). Thank you for checking out this beautiful home that's close to everything San Jose has to offer. Because the house is close to the San Jose airport, Silicon Valley companies, Levi's and Avaya stadiums, SAP Center, The Convention Center, and downtown San Jose it has become a popular place for guests - business people and tourists alike.

Opening up my home to Airbnb guests is very new to me and I'm still learning from every new guest experience and using that experience to make the next guest's stay more comfortable. Examples include: making a bottle of water available for every guest, filling the biscuit barrel with biscuits or chocolates, adding a lock to the room (there wasn't one previously), buying a hair dryer (being a guy I never thought that that some women would ask for it), providing an iron. However, I have spent more than 1,200 nights at a number of hotel chains - Marriott (my favorite), Starwood, The Ritz Carlton, Four Seasons, and have borrowed these experiences in making guest stays more comfortable. While you will find both lower priced and higher priced rooms in the area I price the room based on certain minimum standards required to maintain the place. As a result, you will find that my prices are not quite as low as some of the motels in the area, but they are nowhere as high as a major hotel. If you like a beautiful, clean room, at a reasonable price you will not be disappointed!

Lastly, I'm a big proponent of the "sharing economy" and believe that we need to put more of our assets to work - that includes our homes, our cars, and our time - to create economic opportunities and uplift for all! As an example, much of the proceeds from Airbnb goes towards paying for the upkeep of the house - the groundsman, pool service, and cleaning staff. More people busy and working means lower taxes, less government, and more citizens taking care of their own needs.

During your stay

CARLA  Hi!  I was so blessed to have been raised in South America.  Enjoy traveling all over the world. Graduate of University of California.   I love my teaching job.   I used to do white water rafting in kayaks.   Enjoy boogie boarding and snorkling  in warm waves.  Had a wonderful time raising  our precious kids, dogs and chickens. Love American football  and  soccer seasons.   May the toughest teams win!    
COME RELAX.   Come enjoy our garden in good weather or stay  inside and make yourself comfortable after a long day of sightseeing or working in the Bay Area.  
We will enjoy meeting you and making your journey a great experience. Put us on your Airbnb Wish List and go ahead and reserve your room.

name: Netflix Ready Modern 1 Br Apt w/ Parking & Laundry
description:
WE ARE TAKING EVERY PRECAUTION TO PROTECT OUR GUESTS BY USING CLEANING PRODUCTS THAT ARE ON THE CDC-APPROVED LIST OF DISINFECTANTS.

This entirely private furnished home is ready for you to move in w/your a suitcase. Enjoy coffee on your private outdoor patio, a quick commute to major tech employers, cooking in your kitchen just like at home. You'll also love walking or running at the park down the street & quiet sidewalks right outside your front door to take a stroll.
host_about:
I'm a mid-30's Airbnb Host and Traveler with over a decade in the SF Bay Area, ready to help you find a great home for your short or 1+ month stay. I'm also honored to have over 250 great reviews on Airbnb. While we accept shorter reservations, we specialize in providing furnished homes for 1-12 months, and have noticed many of our customers are business travelers and travel nurses. And we know what they want!

Safe homes with amenities and transportation nearby, close to work, good office chair & desk for working at home, easy check-in without coordinating schedules, large WiFi connected TV's with Netflix to relax, personalized recommendations to meet like-minded folks, access to outdoor and fitness areas... and plenty more. As a former employee traveling for work in the finance industry, I realized that staying in hotels for long periods wasn't all it was chalked up to be... and that I could help provide a better experience for other travelers also. 

I've hosted hundreds of guests from around the US and world, and have studios to 2 bedroom apartments around the San Francisco Bay Area and Silicon Valley: 
- Mountain View
- San Jose
- Redwood City
- Oakland (quick commute to San Francisco)
- Richmond

Send me a message and let's see what we can find closest to your work that meets your needs.

I LOVE the San Francisco Bay Area, and I want you to also! I've lived here for over a decade, and there may be no other place in the world that offers the mix of opportunity, great weather, beautiful nature, urban activities, events, concerts, sporting events, and all kinds of great people.

I'll provide you my own local guide of activities, meetups for your personal interests, and do my best to enjoying your time in the Bay, being productive, staying active, and making the most of your time here (or you're welcome to relax.. we're just here when you need us.)

I have personally stayed in over 25 different Airbnb apartments around the US and the world, so I also know a thing or two about what makes a great furnished home and host. And will do my best to provide that to you. 

A little more about me personally: I've lived in California my whole life, and graduated from San Francisco State University, with a major in Economics and minor in Finance. I've lived all over the Bay Area, including most of the homes I host on Airbnb. I used to work for the State of California in bank regulation, before providing furnished homes and great stays to my guests full-time. 

I enjoy learning and sharing with other Airbnb hosts and real estate investors. In my free time, I also enjoy water color painting, karaoke, beaches, traveling, and making people happy :) 

I realize the San Francisco Bay Area gets very busy and can be quite pricey relative to other locations, so please send me a message so I can see what affordable home we can get you, before everything gets booked up. Thank you for your time.

name: Downtown San Jose SOFA, Rm 3- private room w/ lock
description:
Cozy bedroom (1 of 4) w/ keypad entry, queen bed, small desk, chair, & closet. Shared kitchen & 2 bathrooms if other guests.
Charming SOFA District Gated Victorian (2nd St.) is a 5 minutes walk to Adobe, Zoom, EY, San Jose McEnery Convention Center, Center for Performing Arts, SJ Civic Center, SAP (Sharks hockey & concerts), SJSU, Ca. Theater, Children's Discovery Museum, Tech Museum, Rock Climbing gym, Jui Jitsu & Boxing gyms, yoga studio, SOFA Market, San Pedro Square, restaurants, & bars.
host_about:
I grew up in San Jose (as A child I recall walking with my 3 siblings to school –or the neighborhood community pool during summer - by way of dirt paths meandering through fruit orchards) and watched the Bay Area transform into the Silicon Valley. My Father was an IRS corporate auditor and my Mother a chemist who became the first female on the board of directors for the Santa Clara County Water District, so when we got home from school, we were pretty much on our own to get our homework and chores completed, and the table set before the parents got home from work. We made a meager allowance, so from a young age I couldn't wait to work for a company and receive a real paycheck.

After working my way full-time through school (in my day we didn’t rely on parents or the government to pay for our school and cars) achieving a BS at SJSU, I worked for 5-years at Menlo Park corporate-based Network General Corporation. I was the 75th employee and when I left to launch my own business, there were 5,000 employees and growing. I was a green (it used to define being “naive” and not saving our deteriorating environment) recruit who quickly became a workaholic, with a fierce, decade plus older bipolar boss, often requiring me to work from 6:00am to 9:00pm six days a week. I absorbed a plethora of business acumen during my tenure - the good, the bad, and the ugly. (Boy did these predominantly Stanford grad, baby boomer techies make modern reality shows seem like preschool- as I witnessed in awe affairs, abuse of power, office politics, hidden agendas, revenge - even to the point of violence - and personal vendettas!) Amongst that chaos (movie worthy!), we launched the diagnostic Sniffer network analyzer and provided network training, GURU consulting and CNX certification. 

Our CEO at the time named Harry Saal who I respected, was on the first “internet superhighway” launch committee. (Yes, that is what we first called the World Wide Web). Technology was moving fast. Shortly after I left NGC, they sold to McAfee. I was married in 1993 and created a downtown San Jose graphic design firm MoonCheese Studios, Inc. (was Derksen Design Group prior to incorporating) which ultimately was acquired by Creatus, a backend and application engineering and placement company, while raising two kids now in college (22 & 24). The Creatus CEO made some bad decisions during the dot com bubble burst (right before 911) and closed the business without notice, leaving to India to run a sister division there, leaving many creditors - including us unfortunately! We began freelancing and had a great stint with Thomas Kincade (yes, the painter of light himself) which allowed my husband to travel the nation in private jets while I worked at home with the kids (hmm) and began intensive volunteering at their elementary school serving as VP of Education, art and  science docent, and even literature (Junior Great Books) docent to instruct the students subjects that city budget cuts removed from their school. 

I was also room Mom for both my children’s classes. We later published a glossy, high-end community magazine (doubling as editor and writer) which highlighted local leaders and heroes selflessly improving the neighborhood, while promoting small businesses via advertising and advertorials for 9 years in both 95120 and Los Gatos (distributed collectively to over 18,000 homes with an 80,000 person reach) so I became very well known in the area. I became a board member for the Almaden Valley Business Association (a subset of the the Silicon Valley Chamber of Commerce) and also a member of the Los Gatos Social Club featuring the who is who (such as current and past Mayors and other politicians, philanthropists, business owners, and activists). 

As publisher, it was rewarding to promote charities and feature the passionate founders, while giving many small businesses a marketing boost and coaching them to produce solid advertising campaigns in our publications. 
Then I survived 3 heart-wrenching challenges in a row (at 41 my Father who was my rock and our family glue passed away, at 42 I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and experienced 3 near fatal events like staph during treatment which included 7 surgeries, chemo, radiation and so on, and lastly an economic downturn doubled with a divorce so I went from owning 3 properties to 1, but I made it work. 

I began hosting one room via AirBNB in 2017 to explore the operation, learn the app, and see if I could create a sustainable B&B business model. Three years in, I became addicted to it and absolutely love running my successful downtown San Jose business as a Superhost. I love the hospitality industry!

name: Downtown San Jose, Private, locked Queen Room 1
description:
Spacious bedroom (1 of 4) w/ keypad entry, queen bed, small desk, closet w/ deadbolt. During Winter may have home to yourself!
Charming SOFA District Gated Victorian (2nd St.) is a 5 minutes walk to Adobe, Zoom, EY, San Jose McEnery Convention Center, Center for Performing Arts, SJ Civic Center, SAP (Sharks hockey & concerts), SJSU, Ca. Theater, Children's Discovery Museum, Tech Museum, Rock Climbing gym, Jui Jitsu & Boxing gym, yoga studio, SOFA Market, San Pedro Square, restaurants, & bars.
host_about:
I grew up in San Jose (as A child I recall walking with my 3 siblings to school –or the neighborhood community pool during summer - by way of dirt paths meandering through fruit orchards) and watched the Bay Area transform into the Silicon Valley. My Father was an IRS corporate auditor and my Mother a chemist who became the first female on the board of directors for the Santa Clara County Water District, so when we got home from school, we were pretty much on our own to get our homework and chores completed, and the table set before the parents got home from work. We made a meager allowance, so from a young age I couldn't wait to work for a company and receive a real paycheck.

After working my way full-time through school (in my day we didn’t rely on parents or the government to pay for our school and cars) achieving a BS at SJSU, I worked for 5-years at Menlo Park corporate-based Network General Corporation. I was the 75th employee and when I left to launch my own business, there were 5,000 employees and growing. I was a green (it used to define being “naive” and not saving our deteriorating environment) recruit who quickly became a workaholic, with a fierce, decade plus older bipolar boss, often requiring me to work from 6:00am to 9:00pm six days a week. I absorbed a plethora of business acumen during my tenure - the good, the bad, and the ugly. (Boy did these predominantly Stanford grad, baby boomer techies make modern reality shows seem like preschool- as I witnessed in awe affairs, abuse of power, office politics, hidden agendas, revenge - even to the point of violence - and personal vendettas!) Amongst that chaos (movie worthy!), we launched the diagnostic Sniffer network analyzer and provided network training, GURU consulting and CNX certification. 

Our CEO at the time named Harry Saal who I respected, was on the first “internet superhighway” launch committee. (Yes, that is what we first called the World Wide Web). Technology was moving fast. Shortly after I left NGC, they sold to McAfee. I was married in 1993 and created a downtown San Jose graphic design firm MoonCheese Studios, Inc. (was Derksen Design Group prior to incorporating) which ultimately was acquired by Creatus, a backend and application engineering and placement company, while raising two kids now in college (22 & 24). The Creatus CEO made some bad decisions during the dot com bubble burst (right before 911) and closed the business without notice, leaving to India to run a sister division there, leaving many creditors - including us unfortunately! We began freelancing and had a great stint with Thomas Kincade (yes, the painter of light himself) which allowed my husband to travel the nation in private jets while I worked at home with the kids (hmm) and began intensive volunteering at their elementary school serving as VP of Education, art and  science docent, and even literature (Junior Great Books) docent to instruct the students subjects that city budget cuts removed from their school. 

I was also room Mom for both my children’s classes. We later published a glossy, high-end community magazine (doubling as editor and writer) which highlighted local leaders and heroes selflessly improving the neighborhood, while promoting small businesses via advertising and advertorials for 9 years in both 95120 and Los Gatos (distributed collectively to over 18,000 homes with an 80,000 person reach) so I became very well known in the area. I became a board member for the Almaden Valley Business Association (a subset of the the Silicon Valley Chamber of Commerce) and also a member of the Los Gatos Social Club featuring the who is who (such as current and past Mayors and other politicians, philanthropists, business owners, and activists). 

As publisher, it was rewarding to promote charities and feature the passionate founders, while giving many small businesses a marketing boost and coaching them to produce solid advertising campaigns in our publications. 
Then I survived 3 heart-wrenching challenges in a row (at 41 my Father who was my rock and our family glue passed away, at 42 I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and experienced 3 near fatal events like staph during treatment which included 7 surgeries, chemo, radiation and so on, and lastly an economic downturn doubled with a divorce so I went from owning 3 properties to 1, but I made it work. 

I began hosting one room via AirBNB in 2017 to explore the operation, learn the app, and see if I could create a sustainable B&B business model. Three years in, I became addicted to it and absolutely love running my successful downtown San Jose business as a Superhost. I love the hospitality industry! 

Personal Likes: Besides valuing time children, I enjoy hiking in the woods or to a beach, fine dining, bike riding, puppies, Napa wine tasting, dancing, photography, writing, marketing and promoting, helping others, charity events, world-wide traveling to exotic locations (I traveled constantly for 4 years, becoming an expert in hospitality), learning other cultures, attending concerts, and spending time with close friends, as well as, meeting new ones.

name: Downtown SJ Proper, Private locked Room 2 w/queen
description:
Spacious Room 2 bedroom (1 of 4) w/ keyed entry, queen bed, large work desk, closet w/ deadbolt.
Charming SOFA District Gated Victorian (2nd St.) is a 5 to 10 minutes walk to Adobe, Zoom, EY, San Jose McEnery Convention Center, Center for Performing Arts, SJ Civic Center, SAP (Sharks hockey & concerts), SJSU, Ca. Theater, Children's Discovery Museum, Tech Museum, Rock Climbing gym, Jui Jitsu & Boxing gyms, yoga studio, SOFA Market, San Pedro Square, restaurants, & bars.
host_about:
I grew up in San Jose (as A child I recall walking with my 3 siblings to school –or the neighborhood community pool during summer - by way of dirt paths meandering through fruit orchards) and watched the Bay Area transform into the Silicon Valley. My Father was an IRS corporate auditor and my Mother a chemist who became the first female on the board of directors for the Santa Clara County Water District, so when we got home from school, we were pretty much on our own to get our homework and chores completed, and the table set before the parents got home from work. We made a meager allowance, so from a young age I couldn't wait to work for a company and receive a real paycheck.

After working my way full-time through school (in my day we didn’t rely on parents or the government to pay for our school and cars) achieving a BS at SJSU, I worked for 5-years at Menlo Park corporate-based Network General Corporation. I was the 75th employee and when I left to launch my own business, there were 5,000 employees and growing. I was a green (it used to define being “naive” and not saving our deteriorating environment) recruit who quickly became a workaholic, with a fierce, decade plus older bipolar boss, often requiring me to work from 6:00am to 9:00pm six days a week. I absorbed a plethora of business acumen during my tenure - the good, the bad, and the ugly. (Boy did these predominantly Stanford grad, baby boomer techies make modern reality shows seem like preschool- as I witnessed in awe affairs, abuse of power, office politics, hidden agendas, revenge - even to the point of violence - and personal vendettas!) Amongst that chaos (movie worthy!), we launched the diagnostic Sniffer network analyzer and provided network training, GURU consulting and CNX certification. 

Our CEO at the time named Harry Saal who I respected, was on the first “internet superhighway” launch committee. (Yes, that is what we first called the World Wide Web). Technology was moving fast. Shortly after I left NGC, they sold to McAfee. I was married in 1993 and created a downtown San Jose graphic design firm MoonCheese Studios, Inc. (was Derksen Design Group prior to incorporating) which ultimately was acquired by Creatus, a backend and application engineering and placement company, while raising two kids now in college (22 & 24). The Creatus CEO made some bad decisions during the dot com bubble burst (right before 911) and closed the business without notice, leaving to India to run a sister division there, leaving many creditors - including us unfortunately! We began freelancing and had a great stint with Thomas Kincade (yes, the painter of light himself) which allowed my husband to travel the nation in private jets while I worked at home with the kids (hmm) and began intensive volunteering at their elementary school serving as VP of Education, art and  science docent, and even literature (Junior Great Books) docent to instruct the students subjects that city budget cuts removed from their school. 

I was also room Mom for both my children’s classes. We later published a glossy, high-end community magazine (doubling as editor and writer) which highlighted local leaders and heroes selflessly improving the neighborhood, while promoting small businesses via advertising and advertorials for 9 years in both 95120 and Los Gatos (distributed collectively to over 18,000 homes with an 80,000 person reach) so I became very well known in the area. I became a board member for the Almaden Valley Business Association (a subset of the the Silicon Valley Chamber of Commerce) and also a member of the Los Gatos Social Club featuring the who is who (such as current and past Mayors and other politicians, philanthropists, business owners, and activists). 

As publisher, it was rewarding to promote charities and feature the passionate founders, while giving many small businesses a marketing boost and coaching them to produce solid advertising campaigns in our publications. 
Then I survived 3 heart-wrenching challenges in a row (at 41 my Father who was my rock and our family glue passed away, at 42 I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and experienced 3 near fatal events like staph during treatment which included 7 surgeries, chemo, radiation and so on, and lastly an economic downturn doubled with a divorce so I went from owning 3 properties to 1, but I made it work. 

I began hosting one room via AirBNB in 2017 to explore the operation, learn the app, and see if I could create a sustainable B&B business model. Three years in, I became addicted to it and absolutely love running my successful downtown San Jose business as a Superhost. I love the hospitality industry! 

Personal Likes: Besides valuing time children, I enjoy hiking in the woods or to a beach, fine dining, bike riding, puppies, Napa wine tasting, dancing, photography, writing, marketing and promoting, helping others, charity events, world-wide traveling to exotic locations (I traveled constantly for 4 years, becoming an expert in hospitality), learning other cultures, attending concerts, and spending time with close friends, as well as, meeting new ones.

host_about:
I grew up in San Jose (as A child I recall walking with my 3 siblings to school –or the neighborhood community pool during summer - by way of dirt paths meandering through fruit orchards) and watched the Bay Area transform into the Silicon Valley. My Father was an IRS corporate auditor and my Mother a chemist who became the first female on the board of directors for the Santa Clara County Water District, so when we got home from school, we were pretty much on our own to get our homework and chores completed, and the table set before the parents got home from work. We made a meager allowance, so from a young age I couldn't wait to work for a company and receive a real paycheck.

After working my way full-time through school (in my day we didn’t rely on parents or the government to pay for our school and cars) achieving a BS at SJSU, I worked for 5-years at Menlo Park corporate-based Network General Corporation. I was the 75th employee and when I left to launch my own business, there were 5,000 employees and growing. I was a green (it used to define being “naive” and not saving our deteriorating environment) recruit who quickly became a workaholic, with a fierce, decade plus older bipolar boss, often requiring me to work from 6:00am to 9:00pm six days a week. I absorbed a plethora of business acumen during my tenure - the good, the bad, and the ugly. (Boy did these predominantly Stanford grad, baby boomer techies make modern reality shows seem like preschool- as I witnessed in awe affairs, abuse of power, office politics, hidden agendas, revenge - even to the point of violence - and personal vendettas!) Amongst that chaos (movie worthy!), we launched the diagnostic Sniffer network analyzer and provided network training, GURU consulting and CNX certification. 

Our CEO at the time named Harry Saal who I respected, was on the first “internet superhighway” launch committee. (Yes, that is what we first called the World Wide Web). Technology was moving fast. Shortly after I left NGC, they sold to McAfee. I was married in 1993 and created a downtown San Jose graphic design firm MoonCheese Studios, Inc. (was Derksen Design Group prior to incorporating) which ultimately was acquired by Creatus, a backend and application engineering and placement company, while raising two kids now in college (22 & 24). The Creatus CEO made some bad decisions during the dot com bubble burst (right before 911) and closed the business without notice, leaving to India to run a sister division there, leaving many creditors - including us unfortunately! We began freelancing and had a great stint with Thomas Kincade (yes, the painter of light himself) which allowed my husband to travel the nation in private jets while I worked at home with the kids (hmm) and began intensive volunteering at their elementary school serving as VP of Education, art and  science docent, and even literature (Junior Great Books) docent to instruct the students subjects that city budget cuts removed from their school. 

I was also room Mom for both my children’s classes. We later published a glossy, high-end community magazine (doubling as editor and writer) which highlighted local leaders and heroes selflessly improving the neighborhood, while promoting small businesses via advertising and advertorials for 9 years in both 95120 and Los Gatos (distributed collectively to over 18,000 homes with an 80,000 person reach) so I became very well known in the area. I became a board member for the Almaden Valley Business Association (a subset of the the Silicon Valley Chamber of Commerce) and also a member of the Los Gatos Social Club featuring the who is who (such as current and past Mayors and other politicians, philanthropists, business owners, and activists). 

As publisher, it was rewarding to promote charities and feature the passionate founders, while giving many small businesses a marketing boost and coaching them to produce solid advertising campaigns in our publications. 
Then I survived 3 heart-wrenching challenges in a row (at 41 my Father who was my rock and our family glue passed away, at 42 I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and experienced 3 near fatal events like staph during treatment which included 7 surgeries, chemo, radiation and so on, and lastly an economic downturn doubled with a divorce so I went from owning 3 properties to 1, but I made it work. 

I began hosting one room via AirBNB in 2017 to explore the operation, learn the app, and see if I could create a sustainable B&B business model. Three years in, I became addicted to it and absolutely love running my successful downtown San Jose business as a Superhost. I love the hospitality industry! 

Personal Likes: Besides valuing time children, I enjoy hiking in the woods or to a beach, fine dining, bike riding, puppies, Napa wine tasting, dancing, photography, writing, marketing and promoting, helping others, charity events, world-wide traveling to exotic locations (I traveled constantly for 4 years, becoming an expert in hospitality), learning other cultures, attending concerts, and spending time with close friends, as well as, meeting new ones.

host_about:
Welcome to our home.

It gives me a great pleasure to be your host and I thank you in advance for the oportunity you are giving me to host you!

My background is eastern European, originally moved to Chicago city (still my favorite) and moved to the Bay Area several years ago. I enjoy traveling and one thing I always look for to find when i book for myslef  is the cleanines of the space. Therfore, it is important to me that when you book with us, you will come to a clean, comfortable and quiet home. Please note, our homes are smoke and pet free. (We do not allow smoking in the apartment and we don't allow pets in the apartment).

Please note, we don't provide daily room service (we don't do laundry, we don't make beds, we dont run errands for our guests), if this is your preference,  these services will be provided to you for additional cost.

Hosting has given me an opportunity to communcate with so many wonderful and intelligent people from all over the world,  it has truly been a joy!

 I do appreciate guests who notify me when they are checked in and checked out and update me of any damages that occured during their stay, this avoids unpleasant surprises and inconveniences for my next guests. For example, if the lights are burned out,  oven, microwave,  dishwasher, iron not working,  kitchen sink disposal,  toilet, bathroom and bathtub drainage etc. Occasionally,  I did come acros few surprises and I can't emphasize enough how important this is to me.

One final thing, when booking and you have special requests, please message me in advance so I can work on accomodating you and avoid last minute hassles.

For those of you who had the experience to stay with us, we thank you for being our guest  and hope to see you again in the near future.

And for those who are looking for a place to stay, I encourage you to give us a try and book with us, we will be delighted to host you! 

Cheers!

Sammi

I am the founder of "Another Day in Paradise - A Luxury Vacation Rental Company" which was established in 2017. We partner with Airbnb to provide travelers unique and unforgettable vacation experiences during their stays. Regardless of whether you are on a leisure or a business trip, our goal is to make sure you stay at a relaxing, comfortable, and tranquil space where you would enjoy your best vacation time.

Our mission is to provide homes during times of crisis, and unlock the power of sharing space, resources, and support in times of needs! We partner with the worldwide communities to open housing in emergencies in order to offer shelters for people who lost their homes.

Thank you for reading our story! My team and I can't wait to hosting you in the near future!

host_about:
We have been providing vacation rental apartments for over 10 years across the East Coast. We are known for our distinctively furnished apartments in popular locations, and for our attentive service. You’ll find that our rates are quite reasonable. If you're looking for a safe, comfortable place with fabulous amenities and Wi-Fi (we know you need the Wi-Fi!) in the Boston MA area, Washington DC, Miami FL or very close to NYC in Jersey City or Hoboken, we'd love to host you. Many of the buildings where our apartments are located feature amenities such as beautiful lobbies, 24 hour front desk staff, fitness centers, business centers, recreation rooms, indoor or outdoor pools and whirlpools. If you are traveling with children, some buildings offer playgrounds (many buildings are near public playgrounds as well) or indoor playrooms. Depending on the location, you can stay for just a few days, a week, a month or more. 

We offer an assortment of short-term apartments in sizes ranging from a studio to three bedrooms that are fully furnished with all the comforts of home. Our local staff meticulously prepares your apartment before your arrival, and we offer 24 hour assistance for any emergencies after business hours. When you arrive at your apartment, the beds will be made, towels and bath amenities will be stocked in the bathrooms, and the coffee maker will be set up in the kitchen with some sample coffees, sweetener and creamer (teabags too if that is your preference) to start your morning off properly. If you’d like to cook a meal, the kitchen is stocked with dishes, cutlery, glassware and pots and pans. The living room is set up with a TV and cable channels, and the Wi-Fi router password and instructions will be prominently displayed so you can get connected quickly. You can also make local and toll-free phone calls at no charge. 

Please contact us to confirm the exact availability of the apartment you are interested in. We’d love to host you (and your family) for your vacation or business trip.

My husband retired a few years ago but he prefers to occupy his time by driving rideshare full-time.  My 20-year-old son is attending college.  

I look forward to meeting you.

name: Private, stylish, clean detached studio
description:
Our charming SOFA District Victorian (on 2nd St.) is 5 - 10 minutes walking distance to San Jose McEnery convention center, center for performing arts, SJSU, restaurants, Tech Museum, rock climbing, Ritz & bars. SAP (Sharks & concerts) is a 15 minute walk. (We are in the real downtown perimeter.)

This reservation is for our fully-loaded, newly remodeled detached unit bedroom studio in the back of the home. To add guests beyond 2, requires approval.
host_about:
I grew up in San Jose (as A child I recall walking with my 3 siblings to school –or the neighborhood community pool during summer - by way of dirt paths meandering through fruit orchards) and watched the Bay Area transform into the Silicon Valley. My Father was an IRS corporate auditor and my Mother a chemist who became the first female on the board of directors for the Santa Clara County Water District, so when we got home from school, we were pretty much on our own to get our homework and chores completed, and the table set before the parents got home from work. We made a meager allowance, so from a young age I couldn't wait to work for a company and receive a real paycheck.

After working my way full-time through school (in my day we didn’t rely on parents or the government to pay for our school and cars) achieving a BS at SJSU, I worked for 5-years at Menlo Park corporate-based Network General Corporation. I was the 75th employee and when I left to launch my own business, there were 5,000 employees and growing. I was a green (it used to define being “naive” and not saving our deteriorating environment) recruit who quickly became a workaholic, with a fierce, decade plus older bipolar boss, often requiring me to work from 6:00am to 9:00pm six days a week. I absorbed a plethora of business acumen during my tenure - the good, the bad, and the ugly. (Boy did these predominantly Stanford grad, baby boomer techies make modern reality shows seem like preschool- as I witnessed in awe affairs, abuse of power, office politics, hidden agendas, revenge - even to the point of violence - and personal vendettas!) Amongst that chaos (movie worthy!), we launched the diagnostic Sniffer network analyzer and provided network training, GURU consulting and CNX certification. 

Our CEO at the time named Harry Saal who I respected, was on the first “internet superhighway” launch committee. (Yes, that is what we first called the World Wide Web). Technology was moving fast. Shortly after I left NGC, they sold to McAfee. I was married in 1993 and created a downtown San Jose graphic design firm MoonCheese Studios, Inc. (was Derksen Design Group prior to incorporating) which ultimately was acquired by Creatus, a backend and application engineering and placement company, while raising two kids now in college (22 & 24). The Creatus CEO made some bad decisions during the dot com bubble burst (right before 911) and closed the business without notice, leaving to India to run a sister division there, leaving many creditors - including us unfortunately! I began hosting one room via AirBNB in 2017 to explore the operation, learn the app, and see if I could create a sustainable B&B business model. Three years in, I became addicted to it and absolutely love running my successful downtown San Jose business as a Superhost. I love the hospitality industry! 

Personal Likes: Besides valuing time children, I enjoy hiking in the woods or to a beach, fine dining, bike riding, puppies, Napa wine tasting, dancing, photography, writing, marketing and promoting, helping others, charity events, world-wide traveling to exotic locations (I traveled constantly for 4 years, becoming an expert in hospitality), learning other cultures, attending concerts, and spending time with close friends, as well as, meeting new ones.

name: The Parlor Room-Cozy Queen bedroom w lock downtown
description:
Spacious key entry room (1 of 4) w/ queen bed, dresser, 70 inch TV, & armoire.
Charming SOFA District Gated Victorian (2nd St.) is a 5 to 10 minute walk to Adobe, Zoom, EY, San Jose McEnery Convention Center, Center for Performing Arts, SJ Civic Center, SAP (Sharks hockey & concerts), SJSU, Ca. Theater, Children's Discovery Museum, Tech Museum, Rock Climbing gym, Jui Jitsu & Boxing gyms, yoga studio, SOFA Market, San Pedro Square, restaurants, & bars.
host_about:
I grew up in San Jose (as A child I recall walking with my 3 siblings to school –or the neighborhood community pool during summer - by way of dirt paths meandering through fruit orchards) and watched the Bay Area transform into the Silicon Valley. My Father was an IRS corporate auditor and my Mother a chemist who became the first female on the board of directors for the Santa Clara County Water District, so when we got home from school, we were pretty much on our own to get our homework and chores completed, and the table set before the parents got home from work. We made a meager allowance, so from a young age I couldn't wait to work for a company and receive a real paycheck.

After working my way full-time through school (in my day we didn’t rely on parents or the government to pay for our school and cars) achieving a BS at SJSU, I worked for 5-years at Menlo Park corporate-based Network General Corporation. I was the 75th employee and when I left to launch my own business, there were 5,000 employees and growing. I was a green (it used to define being “naive” and not saving our deteriorating environment) recruit who quickly became a workaholic, with a fierce, decade plus older bipolar boss, often requiring me to work from 6:00am to 9:00pm six days a week. I absorbed a plethora of business acumen during my tenure - the good, the bad, and the ugly. (Boy did these predominantly Stanford grad, baby boomer techies make modern reality shows seem like preschool- as I witnessed in awe affairs, abuse of power, office politics, hidden agendas, revenge - even to the point of violence - and personal vendettas!) Amongst that chaos (movie worthy!), we launched the diagnostic Sniffer network analyzer and provided network training, GURU consulting and CNX certification. 

Our CEO at the time named Harry Saal who I respected, was on the first “internet superhighway” launch committee. (Yes, that is what we first called the World Wide Web). Technology was moving fast. Shortly after I left NGC, they sold to McAfee. I was married in 1993 and created a downtown San Jose graphic design firm MoonCheese Studios, Inc. (was Derksen Design Group prior to incorporating) which ultimately was acquired by Creatus, a backend and application engineering and placement company, while raising two kids now in college (22 & 24). The Creatus CEO made some bad decisions during the dot com bubble burst (right before 911) and closed the business without notice, leaving to India to run a sister division there, leaving many creditors - including us unfortunately! We began freelancing and had a great stint with Thomas Kincade (yes, the painter of light himself) which allowed my husband to travel the nation in private jets while I worked at home with the kids (hmm) and began intensive volunteering at their elementary school serving as VP of Education, art and  science docent, and even literature (Junior Great Books) docent to instruct the students subjects that city budget cuts removed from their school. 

I was also room Mom for both my children’s classes. We later published a glossy, high-end community magazine (doubling as editor and writer) which highlighted local leaders and heroes selflessly improving the neighborhood, while promoting small businesses via advertising and advertorials for 9 years in both 95120 and Los Gatos (distributed collectively to over 18,000 homes with an 80,000 person reach) so I became very well known in the area. I became a board member for the Almaden Valley Business Association (a subset of the the Silicon Valley Chamber of Commerce) and also a member of the Los Gatos Social Club featuring the who is who (such as current and past Mayors and other politicians, philanthropists, business owners, and activists). 

As publisher, it was rewarding to promote charities and feature the passionate founders, while giving many small businesses a marketing boost and coaching them to produce solid advertising campaigns in our publications. 
Then I survived 3 heart-wrenching challenges in a row (at 41 my Father who was my rock and our family glue passed away, at 42 I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and experienced 3 near fatal events like staph during treatment which included 7 surgeries, chemo, radiation and so on, and lastly an economic downturn doubled with a divorce so I went from owning 3 properties to 1, but I made it work. 

I began hosting one room via AirBNB in 2017 to explore the operation, learn the app, and see if I could create a sustainable B&B business model. Three years in, I became addicted to it and absolutely love running my successful downtown San Jose business as a Superhost. I love the hospitality industry! 

Personal Likes: Besides valuing time children, I enjoy hiking in the woods or to a beach, fine dining, bike riding, puppies, Napa wine tasting, dancing, photography, writing, marketing and promoting, helping others, charity events, world-wide traveling to exotic locations (I traveled constantly for 4 years, becoming an expert in hospitality), learning other cultures, attending concerts, and spending time with close friends, as well as, meeting new ones.

host_about:
I am the founder of "Another Day in Paradise - A Luxury Vacation Rental Company" which was established in 2017. We partner with Airbnb to provide travelers unique and unforgettable vacation experiences during their stays. Regardless of whether you are on a leisure or a business trip, our goal is to make sure you stay at a relaxing, comfortable, and tranquil space where you would enjoy your best vacation time.

We have over 25 vacation rental properties throughout California, including Bay Area, Pacific Grove, Half Moon Bay, Chico, Clear Lake and South Lake Tahoe. We own all of our properties in order to provide the highest quality of service. 

When I travel, I always stay at Airbnb properties. I personally have very high expectations when staying away from home, and I hope all our properties meet yours, knowing you are traveling away from your home. My team members include my partner, Carrie, a customer service crew, a cleaning crew and a repair / handyman crew. They are on call 7-days a week at your service. We strive to exceed expectations to all of our guests with the utmost respect and respond. We will ensure each property is thoroughly cleaned with enhanced cleaning protocols, and with fresh bed sheets, towels, and bath rugs upon your arrival.

I am also an active member of Airbnb.org which is a non-profit organization started by the founders of Airbnb. On a daily basis, we donate a certain percentage of our revenue from each guest's booking to Airbnb.org. Our mission is to provide homes during times of crisis, and unlock the power of sharing space, resources, and support in times of needs! We partner with the worldwide communities to open housing in emergencies in order to offer shelters for people who lost their homes.

Thank you for reading our story! My team and I can't wait to hosting you in the near future!

name: Cozy TwinHaven Perfect 4 Sharing
description:
Welcome to Mt. View. Fully furnished and ready for your arrival. Benefit from a swift commute to major tech employers. Your kitchen, equipped just like home, is perfect for preparing your favorite meals.

host_about:
I'm a mid-30's Airbnb Host and Traveler with over a decade in the SF Bay Area, ready to help you find a great home for your short or 1+ month stay. I'm also honored to have over 250 great reviews on Airbnb. While we accept shorter reservations, we specialize in providing furnished homes for 1-12 months, and have noticed many of our customers are business travelers and travel nurses. And we know what they want!

Safe homes with amenities and transportation nearby, close to work, good office chair & desk for working at home, easy check-in without coordinating schedules, large WiFi connected TV's with Netflix to relax, personalized recommendations to meet like-minded folks, access to outdoor and fitness areas... and plenty more. As a former employee traveling for work in the finance industry, I realized that staying in hotels for long periods wasn't all it was chalked up to be... and that I could help provide a better experience for other travelers also. 

I've hosted hundreds of guests from around the US and world, and have studios to 2 bedroom apartments around the San Francisco Bay Area and Silicon Valley: 
- Mountain View
- San Jose
- Redwood City
- Oakland (quick commute to San Francisco)
- Richmond

Send me a message and let's see what we can find closest to your work that meets your needs.

I LOVE the San Francisco Bay Area, and I want you to also! I've lived here for over a decade, and there may be no other place in the world that offers the mix of opportunity, great weather, beautiful nature, urban activities, events, concerts, sporting events, and all kinds of great people.

I'll provide you my own local guide of activities, meetups for your personal interests, and do my best to enjoying your time in the Bay, being productive, staying active, and making the most of your time here (or you're welcome to relax.. we're just here when you need us.)

I have personally stayed in over 25 different Airbnb apartments around the US and the world, so I also know a thing or two about what makes a great furnished home and host. And will do my best to provide that to you. 

A little more about me personally: I've lived in California my whole life, and graduated from San Francisco State University, with a major in Economics and minor in Finance. I've lived all over the Bay Area, including most of the homes I host on Airbnb. I used to work for the State of California in bank regulation, before providing furnished homes and great stays to my guests full-time. 

I enjoy learning and sharing with other Airbnb hosts and real estate investors. In my free time, I also enjoy water color painting, karaoke, beaches, traveling, and making people happy :) 

I realize the San Francisco Bay Area gets very busy and can be quite pricey relative to other locations, so please send me a message so I can see what affordable home we can get you, before everything gets booked up. Thank you for your time.
